summary: Enterprise AI in 2026 centers on managed model-aggregation platforms that let corporations consume foundation models (GPT, Claude, Llama, Gemini, Mistral, and more) through secure APIs within their own cloud boundary, so prompts and data never leave their governed environment. There is no single winner — the best fit is driven by existing cloud footprint, required model breadth, compliance posture, and billing relationships. AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI/Foundry, and Google Vertex AI dominate adoption, with Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx, Databricks, Oracle, and Cloudflare serving data-platform-native and specialized needs.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts, completions, and fine-tuning data stay inside the enterprise's cloud tenant/VPC and are not used to train base models, satisfying confidentiality and sovereignty requirements.

Compliance and governance: inherit the cloud provider's certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR, PCI-DSS) plus centralized IAM, audit logging, and content-safety controls instead of auditing each model vendor separately.

Consolidated billing and existing contracts: pay through existing cloud committed-spend/EDP agreements, draw down enterprise discount commitments, and avoid onboarding many separate vendor procurement and payment relationships.

Single API and model choice: access many competing models (Claude, Llama, Mistral, GPT, Gemini, Nova, etc.) behind one managed API, enabling model switching and multi-model routing without re-architecting integrations.

Operational integration and security: native tie-in to cloud networking (PrivateLink/VPC), KMS encryption, identity, observability, and data platforms — reducing data egress, latency, and the attack surface of calling public vendor endpoints.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (on-demand) with Provisioned Throughput options; billed through AWS account/EDP. No markup charge for base model usage beyond model rates.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises already on AWS wanting the widest third-party model choice (especially Claude) behind one API.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
available_models: Models-as-a-Service catalog (Llama, Mistral, Cohere, others via Foundry)
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (PTU - Provisioned Throughput Units or pay-as-you-go); billed through Azure Enterprise Agreement / committed spend.
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first shops needing frontier OpenAI models with enterprise governance and M365 integration.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token or throughput reservations via GSUs (Generative AI Scale Units, e.g. ~25 GSUs ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec for Gemini 2.5 Flash); billed through GCP commitments.
platforms.best_for: Data/ML-mature teams on GCP wanting Gemini plus a broad model garden and tight BigQuery/data integration.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits; runs within the Snowflake account/region.
platforms.best_for: Organizations with data gravity in Snowflake wanting LLMs to run directly against governed warehouse data.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Subscription + consumption (Resource Units); on-cloud, on-prem, or hybrid deployment.
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises needing strong AI governance, hybrid/on-prem control, and multi-platform agent management.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs); runs within the customer's lakehouse/cloud account.
platforms.best_for: Data engineering/ML teams on the lakehouse wanting unified governance across data and custom/foundation models.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-character/token or dedicated AI clusters; billed via OCI, with sovereign cloud options.
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric and sovereignty-focused enterprises integrating GenAI with Oracle applications and databases.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use (neurons/requests); serverless with free tier, edge-distributed.
key_features: AI Gateway (caching, rate limiting, logging, model routing)
platforms.best_for: Developers and companies wanting low-latency, globally distributed, cost-efficient inference at the edge.
